record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Let X be a smooth acyclic surface with the property that for every non-constant regular function p in C[X] there exists another regular function q in C[X] such that the morphism F=(p,q): X -> C^2 is proper. Must X be isomorphic to C^2?

evidence.quote:
OUESTION. Let X be a smooth acyclic surface such that for any non–constant
regular function p ∈ C[X] there exists another one q ∈ C[X] with the property that
F = (p, q) : X → C2
is a proper morphism. Is it true that X is isomorphic to C2
?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex algebraic surface that is acyclic (i.e., has trivial reduced singular homology with integer coefficients: $\tilde{H}_*(X;\mathbb{Z})=0$). Suppose $X$ has the following property: for every non-constant regular function $p \in \mathbb{C}[X]$, there exists a regular function $q \in \mathbb{C}[X]$ such that the morphism 
$$F=(p,q):X\longrightarrow \mathbb{C}^2$$
is proper. Must $X$ be isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^2$ as an algebraic variety?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches on characterizations of the affine plane via properties of regular functions and properness conditions on smooth acyclic (topologically contractible) surfaces did not reveal a definitive resolution of this specific question. Related characterizations of $\mathbb{C}^2$ (e.g., via simply connected curves or isotrivial families) are known, but no source directly confirms a positive or negative answer to this exact question.

status_evidence.title: Challenging problems on affine n-space
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems on affine n-space including characterizations of C^2 among acyclic/contractible surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization problems for C^2 among acyclic surfaces were listed as open challenging problems.

status_evidence.title: Isotrivial families of curves on affine surfaces and characterization of the affine plane
status_evidence.snippet: Zaidenberg characterizes C^2 as smooth acyclic surfaces admitting certain families of curves, distinguishing from Ramanujam surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related but distinct characterizations of C^2 among smooth acyclic surfaces are known.
